costa-brava.name: Costa Brava
costa-brava.info:
Runs from: Blanes to the French border at Portbou.

The Costa Brava is in Catalonia. The name means "wild coast", and it fits. Pine-covered cliffs drop into small coves, called calas, with clear green water.

costa-del-maresme.name: Costa del Maresme
costa-del-maresme.info:
Runs from: Montgat, just north of Barcelona, to the Tordera river near Malgrat de Mar.

The Costa del Maresme is in Catalonia, immediately north of Barcelona. It's a long stretch of Mediterranean coastline backed by pine-covered hills, with broad sandy beaches and a string of towns connected by the R1 commuter railway. Calella is the main resort town, with plenty of hotels, bars and nightlife.

costa-de-barcelona.name: Costa de Barcelona
costa-de-barcelona.info:
Runs from: Cunit, a little south-west of Sitges, to the Tordera river near Blanes.

The Costa de Barcelona is in Catalonia. This is Barcelona's own coast, made up of two stretches. Sitges is a fun, friendly beach town with a big LGBTQ+ scene, and it's about 40 minutes from Barcelona by train.

costa-dorada.name: Costa Dorada
costa-dorada.info:
Runs from: Alcanar, near the Valencia border, to Cunit.

The Costa Dorada is in Catalonia. The "golden coast" is famous for its long, golden, sandy beaches. The water is shallow and warm, so it suits families and beginners.

costa-del-azahar.name: Costa del Azahar
costa-del-azahar.info:
Runs from: Vinaròs, at the Catalan border, to Almenara, where Castellón meets Valencia province.

The Costa del Azahar is in Valencia. The "orange blossom coast" is quieter than its neighbours and mostly full of Spanish holidaymakers, so prices stay low. Peñíscola has a castle on a rocky headland, and it starred in Game of Thrones.

costa-de-valencia.name: Costa de Valencia
costa-de-valencia.info:
Runs from: Canet d'en Berenguer, north of Valencia city, to Oliva, near the Alicante border.

The Costa de Valencia is in Valencia. Valencia is the star here, a big, sunny city with a free beach at the end of the tram line. It's the home of paella, and you can try the real thing in the rice fields of the nearby Albufera lagoon.

costa-blanca.name: Costa Blanca
costa-blanca.info:
Runs from: Pilar de la Horadada, at the Murcia border, to Dénia.

The Costa Blanca is in Valencia, in Alicante province. The "white coast" is one of Spain's best-known holiday stretches. Benidorm is a forest of skyscrapers with huge clubs and cheap drinks, and it's a wild stag and hen party town.

costa-calida.name: Costa Cálida
costa-calida.info:
Runs from: Pilar de la Horadada, at the Alicante border, to Águilas, at the Almería border.

The Costa Cálida is in Murcia. The "warm coast" has the Mar Menor, Europe's biggest saltwater lagoon, with shallow, warm, calm water. A thin strip of land called La Manga separates it from the open sea.

costa-de-almeria.name: Costa de Almería
costa-de-almeria.info:
Runs from: The Murcia border, near Pulpí, to Adra.

The Costa de Almería is in Andalusia. Spain's driest, sunniest and emptiest coast. Cabo de Gata-Níjar Natural Park has desert hills, volcanic rock and wild beaches like Los Genoveses and Mónsul.

costa-tropical.name: Costa Tropical
costa-tropical.info:
Runs from: The Almería border, near La Rábita, to Cerro Gordo, near La Herradura, where Málaga begins.

The Costa Tropical is in Andalusia, in Granada province. A short, steep, quiet coast with a mild climate where sugar cane, avocados and custard apples grow. Salobreña is a white village under a castle.

costa-del-sol.name: Costa del Sol
costa-del-sol.info:
Runs from: Manilva, at the Cádiz border, to Nerja, at the Granada border.

The Costa del Sol is in Andalusia, in Málaga province. Spain's most famous coast, with the cheap flights to match. Málaga is a proper city, with a castle, art, great nightlife and grilled sardines on skewers, called espetos, cooked on the beach.

costa-de-la-luz.name: Costa de la Luz
costa-de-la-luz.info:
Runs from: Ayamonte, at the Portuguese border, to Tarifa.

The Costa de la Luz is in Andalusia, in Huelva and Cádiz provinces. The "coast of light" faces the Atlantic, so there are big waves, wide beaches and a lot of wind. Tarifa is Spain's kitesurfing capital, and from there you can take a ferry to Morocco.

rias-baixas.name: Rías Baixas
rias-baixas.info:
Runs from: A Guarda, at the Portuguese border, to the Ría de Muros e Noia.

The Rías Baixas are in Galicia. Four deep sea inlets, called rías, cut into the coast here. The seafood is superb, and it comes with crisp Albariño white wine.

costa-da-morte.name: Costa da Morte
costa-da-morte.info:
Runs from: Around Muros and Fisterra to Malpica. Sources disagree on the exact ends.

The Costa da Morte is in Galicia. The "coast of death" got its name from the many ships wrecked on its rocks. Today it's wild, empty and beautiful.

rias-altas.name: Rías Altas
rias-altas.info:
Runs from: Malpica and A Coruña to Ribadeo, at the Asturian border.

The Rías Altas are in Galicia. The northern rías have huge cliffs and green hills. A Coruña is a lively port city with a Roman lighthouse, the Tower of Hercules, that is still working today.

costa-verde.name: Costa Verde
costa-verde.info:
Runs from: Ribadeo, at the Galician border, to the Deva river, at the Cantabrian border.

The Costa Verde is in Asturias. The "green coast" gets its name from the rain, and the hills are bright green. Gijón is a fun city with a city beach, surf, student bars and cider poured from a great height.

costa-de-cantabria.name: Costa de Cantabria
costa-de-cantabria.info:
Runs from: The Deva river to Castro Urdiales, at the Basque border.

The Costa de Cantabria is in Cantabria. A friendly, relaxed coast with big beaches and green hills. Santander is an easy, elegant city with the beaches of El Sardinero.

costa-vasca.name: Costa Vasca
costa-vasca.info:
Runs from: Castro Urdiales boundary at the Cantabrian border to Hondarribia, at the French border.

The Costa Vasca is in the Basque Country. Wild cliffs, surf beaches and some of the best food in Spain. San Sebastián has a famous city beach and bars full of pintxos, which are small snacks served on bread.
